one_liner: Asana has a broad self-serve REST API with OAuth2 and PATs, free-tier access, and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (PKCE, one-hour tokens, refresh, scopes) for multi-user apps; personal access tokens from the developer console; Enterprise service account tokens (a long-lived static token type, Enterprise only).
access_notes: Free Personal plan includes API access at 150 req/min. Task search, portfolios and goals need a paid plan. A developer sandbox with paid features is free on request.
blocker_notes: Minor: some endpoints (search, portfolios, goals) are paid-only; service accounts are Enterprise only.

evidence.quote: Asana's API is a REST interface that speaks JSON at `https://app.asana.com/api/1.0`
Any user creates a personal access token or an OAuth app in the developer console, with no app review unless the app is listed in the app directory.
To quickly authorize your API requests, create a [personal access token](https://developers.asana.com/docs/personal-access-token) via the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps)
Limits are based on minute-long windows and differ depending on whether the domain is free or paid
Free Personal plan for up to two users, which includes API access at 150 requests a minute.
The Asana V2 MCP server is generally available and uses OAuth for authorization.
The Asana MCP V2 server is available at: `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`.
